Description: Identified a GitLab Personal Access Token, risking unauthorized access to GitLab repositories and codebase exposure.
Author: Nitjsefnie
Message:
Prove the GitLab commit-read failure at the fold boundary

A merged merge request whose merge-request reads succeed but whose
/merge_requests/<iid>/commits read answers 401/403 must reach the
reconcile caller as the credential failure it is — through the sponsor
gateway as ForgeCredentialRejectedError with the linked identity marked
and the run failed with the fixed credential sentence, through the
plain path as the propagating GitLabApiError — and must never produce a
completed run whose fold was computed with finalCommitAt = null. The
healthy control settles the very same merge request once the read
answers, so the two failures fail for the status and nothing else.

Demonstrated against the pre-fix behavior by reverting only the task-1
client hunk: all three failure cases then resolve, completing a run
whose fold silently refused the merge request.

Task 2 of 2 against issue 695.

Co-Authored-By: GLM-5.3-Flash <noreply@z.ai>

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Nitjsefnie
Message:
Pin the persisted credential binding format and share the store key set

Every earlier test sealed and opened through the same binding builder, so
renaming the associated-data domain, reordering the forge row key or
binding the forge token to another column still round-tripped while
leaving every stored v2 credential undecryptable. A known-answer case per
constructor now seals with raw node:crypto under the literal specified
associated data and a separately computed key id, and requires the
constructor's binding to open it.

Also pins isEnvelopeCurrent's part count, and at the store level that a
new webhook secret is sealed under the current key while a previous key is
configured. The webhook binding lowercases its credential id, since the
column is a Postgres uuid that reads back lowercase. The three stores now
build their key set through one tokenKeySetFrom helper.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Nitjsefnie
Message:
test(repositories): pin the production GitLab route wiring through POST and DELETE (refs #547)

Every other route test stubs the registration dependencies, so nothing
executed the limb of buildRegistrationDependencies that hands a GitLab
registration GITLAB_WEBHOOK_URL rather than the GitHub callback and reads the
sponsor's PAT through PostgresForgeIdentityStore; a mutant that always used
the GitHub URL and dropped getForgeToken survived the suite. Two tests now
drive the exported POST and DELETE handlers against Postgres prototype spies,
a stubbed environment carrying both callbacks, and a captured GitLab fetch:
the hook-creation body's url is the GitLab receiver, and the unregistration's
hook DELETE goes out under the token the identity store returned.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Description: Identified a GitLab Personal Access Token, risking unauthorized access to GitLab repositories and codebase exposure.
Author: Nitjsefnie
Message:
feat(fold): mark a rejected GitLab credential at the sponsor-gateway seam (refs #551)

sponsorGateway's GitLab branch wraps every read: a GitLabApiError with
status 401/403 calls the injected markCredentialRejected (best-effort — a
marking failure is logged and the original error rethrown) and surfaces as
the new ForgeCredentialRejectedError, whose message is a fixed sentence
carrying no upstream text. Every other failure class rethrows untouched,
and GitHub folds are never guarded. Wired in instrumentation-node.ts to
PostgresForgeIdentityStore.markTokenRejected through the same identity
store the token resolver uses.

Co-Authored-By: GLM-5.3-Flash <noreply@z.ai>
